messages:
matt: quick follow-up from the GQA/MQA RFC — saw two customer cases where the runtime flipped to GQA and tail latency spiked for mixed short+long queries. can we sanity-check the switch heuristics?
sophia: yeah saw that. current rule is pretty simple: if batch_size >= 2 and avg_seq_len < 128 we favor MQA, otherwise GQA. it's blind to variance.
raj: that variance is exactly the problem. customers send bursts: 8 short queries + 1 long one and GQA wins on avg cost but loses on tail because KV cache thrash.
jenny: also quantization changes kernel memory working set. MQA with q4x4 kept KV contiguous; GQA path did small-chunk allocations and caused >1.2GB extra peak.
matt: concrete ask — do we: (A) improve selector to consider seq_len variance and largest_seq, (B) add a cache-pressure check before switching, or (C) always prefer MQA when there are >N small queries per batch? votes? :thumbsup:
sophia: leaning toward A+B. heuristic idea: score = alpha * expected_compute + beta * expected_kv_pressure + gamma * tail_penalty. pick kernel with lower score. simple fallback: if max_seq_len / avg_seq_len > 3 then prefer MQA.
raj: +1 for max/avg rule. also suggest sampling per-request prefix hit-rate from KV cache stats (recent 30s) and bias toward kernel that preserves contiguous KV layout when hit_rate < 0.6.
jenny: note: need an escape hatch for low-memory hosts. if host_free_gpu_mem < 1.5GB prefer GQA because MQA prefetch can OOM on old cards. add that to scoring.
matt: can someone mock up the scoring formula? we should keep it cheap to compute in hot path.
sophia: draft formula (cheap ops only):
```
score_mqa = w1 * est_tokens_mqa + w2 * (1 - kv_hit_rate) + w3 * max_seq_ratio
score_gqa = w1 * est_tokens_gqa + w2 * kv_allocation_penalty + w3 * tail_penalty
choose = argmin(score)
```
where est_tokens_* is batch_estimated_tokens/throughput_factor (precomputed per-model), kv_* are moving averages, max_seq_ratio = max_seq_len/avg_seq_len. all weights tunable via config.
matt: runtime-bot can we get a CI microbench with mixed distributions: 90% seq=32, 10% seq=1024 across batch sizes 4,8,16 and run both selector A (current) vs selector B (new score) ?
runtime-bot: perf CI queued: job 45321. baseline: current-selector. variant: variance-aware scoring. expect ~30m. link: https://ci.example/45321 (test metadata).
raj: one more edge: model-compiled kernels differ across device. compile-time flags can make MQA slower on older cudnn versions. we need a device compatibility matrix check in selector.
sophia: agreed. add binary compatibility check: if model_kernel_capabilities[device] missing optimized MQA kernels, treat MQA_score += big_penalty.
jenny: also add telemetry labels when selector flips in-flight: we need per-request label `selector_reason` to debug customer regressions. short enums: SIZE_VARIANCE, KV_PRESSURE, MEM_LOW, KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE.
matt: that will help postmortems. final step: I'll open a tiny RFC PR with scoring, flags, and telemetry. can we iterate on numbers after CI results?
sophia: sounds good. I'll prototype the selector in eng-runtime branch/selector-variance and drop a perf patch for the CI job.
raj: I'll add device kernel availability table to infra artifacts so selector can consult it at startup.
jenny: I'll add unit tests around OOM and quantized layout interactions.
matt: thanks all. backlog item: add canary that disables auto-switching for Dedicated customers for 2 weeks while we tune. :white_check_mark:
